body: Hashir Shaikh's us-vs-them thesis: his team makes 1,000+ statics a month, ~10% are us vs them — because showing the difference beats talking about the product. 'Better quality' means nothing without context; an us-vs-them ad supplies it. Compare on one thing that matters — price, ingredients, time, results, quality, convenience — and make the difference obvious. When people see what's different and why it matters, the product becomes easy to understand.
idea: Us-vs-them works because 'better' means nothing without context — compare on ONE thing that matters and make it obvious.
sequencing: The volume: 1,000+ statics a month, ~10% us vs them.
The principle: showing the difference beats talking about the product.
The problem: 'better quality' means nothing without context.
The fix: compare on one thing — price, ingredients, time, results, quality, convenience.
The payoff: the difference obvious, the product easy to understand.
why_it_works: Context is comprehension — a single-axis visual comparison is understood in one glance.
what_to_steal: LC's us-vs-them rule: one comparison axis per static — waterproof vs not, tarnish-free vs green skin — made visually obvious.
